governing: weld_base_metal (bracket plate base metal in shear rupture along the welds, AISC 360-22 J2.4(a)): demand 4.763 kip/in, capacity 4.875 kip/in
notes: Design: a 1/4 in A572 Gr 50 bracket plate set on edge on the W12x40 (A992) column flange, 19 in long along the column, with 3/16 in E70 fillet welds on both sides over the full 19 in, and the 48.42 kip service shear (ASD) applied 5 in from the weld line. Petra check is PASS, with 7 of 7 obligations certified: base metal 0.977, weld 0.855 (elastic method, no directional increase), plate lateral-torsional buckling per F11 0.741, shear yield 0.51, flexural yield 0.358, minimum fillet size 0.667, flange fit 0.078. Centre the plate on the column flange, over the web. Petra does not check the column's local limit states. My hand checks of them, with the plate centred over the web: J10.1 flange local bending need not be checked, because the loaded width of 0.625 in is less than 0.15 bf = 1.20 in; web local yielding is about 0.16 and web crippling about 0.17 under the moment couple of about 19 kip; base metal shear rupture of the column flange along the welds is 0.47. Not covered: how the load is delivered to the plate at the 5 in eccentricity (the plate must project far enough for that detail), and the W12x40 column member under the added 242 kip-in moment, which belong to the beam-side and column designs. The grade was chosen for weight: an A36 plate would need 1/4 x 20-1/4 in or 5/16 x 18 in, and the first trial, 1/2 x 14 in A36 with 5/16 in welds, also passed at 0.94 but is heavier.
